title: BQ-LoRA: Binary-Quantized Low-Rank Adapters as Implicit Regularizers for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2611.22334v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of quantized large language models is dominated by QLoRA, which combines 4-bit weight quantization with FP16 low-rank adapters. We ask whether the FP16 adapter precision is necessary. Replacing it with a single binary bit per adapter parameter, combined with a learned per-layer scale $s$ and a Scaled Straight-Through Estimator, reduces adapter storage by 13-16x. We introduce two variants -- NormScale, which binarizes under a norm-preserving scale with a clipped STE, and LearnThresh, which makes the binarization threshold learnable -- unified under a framework we call BQ-LoRA. Our main theoretical contribution is a tight characterization of the BQ-LoRA hypothesis class: it has bounded entrywise norm, a typical-set spectral norm bound that is $\Theta(r)$ times sharper than the worst case, a full-rank, near-isotropic update, and consequently a Rademacher complexity that yields an explicit $\tilde{O}(s_{\max}\

translated_title: BQ-LoRA：作为参数高效微调隐式正则化器的二值量化低秩适配器
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.22334v1 公告类型：新 摘要：量化大语言模型的参数高效微调目前由 QLoRA 主导，该方法将 4 比特权重量化与 FP16 低秩适配器相结合。我们提出一个问题：FP16 适配器精度是否必要？将每个适配器参数替换为单个二值比特，并结合可学习的逐层缩放因子 $s$ 和缩放直通估计器，可将适配器存储降低 13-16 倍。我们引入两个变体——NormScale，在保持范数的缩放下使用截断 STE 进行二值化；以及 LearnThresh，使二值化阈值可学习——并将它们统一在我们称为 BQ-LoRA 的框架之下。我们的主要理论贡献是对 BQ-LoRA 假设类的紧致刻画：它具有有界的逐元素范数、一个比最坏情况紧 $\Theta(r)$ 倍的典型集谱范数界、满秩的近各向同性更新，因此其 Rademacher 复杂度给出了显式的 $\tilde{O}(s_{\max}\...\）界（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出 BQ-LoRA 框架，将 LoRA 适配器参数量化为单个二值比特并配合可学习的逐层缩放因子与直通估计器，在将适配器存储降低 13-16 倍的同时，从理论上刻画了其假设类的谱范数界与 Rademacher 复杂度，证明二值适配器可作为隐式正则化器实现参数高效微调。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes BQ-LoRA, a framework that binarizes LoRA adapter parameters to a single bit with learned per-layer scales and a scaled straight-through estimator, reducing adapter storage by 13-16x while tightly characterizing its hypothesis class via spectral norm bounds and Rademacher complexity, showing binary adapters act as implicit regularizers for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
